subject: Re: Packaging options for Q4 pilot — tradeoffs and approval path
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging options for pilot — questions on flexibility and downgrade path

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency profile and the built-in eval hooks. Before we move procurement forward, a couple of practical questions on packaging so we can align internally:

1) If we start on the Compact Plus bundle for a 3-month pilot, can we downgrade to Compact mid-contract if we hit usage/latency tradeoffs? Is there a defined downgrade window and how are credits/prorations handled?

2) Are features (live KV caching, real-time tracing, additional eval retention) available as add-ons outside the bundle, or do some require moving to the Elastic tier?

3) For pilot pricing you mentioned a promotional discount — can you share the SOW + a price table that shows both the pilot discount and list prices (we need that for our budget docs)?

We have a procurement lead (procure@clearlinehealth.com) who will want the exact SOW and terms. Goal is to sign something by the end of the month to start before year-end.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of Data & Automation
Clearline Health

Attachments: (none referenced)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options for pilot — questions on flexibility and downgrade path

Hi Anna — great to hear. Short answers up front, full detail below and attached: Redwood_Pricing_Table_Q4.xlsx and a draft SOW.

1) Downgrade path: Yes — we support a single permitted downgrade in a 12-month commitment after a 60-day lock-in. Downgrades are prorated on remaining committed spend; we apply a one-time administrative credit to avoid retro invoice adjustments. We can make the 60-day window shorter for pilots, but that requires a slightly higher pilot discount carve.

2) Feature coupling: Some advanced features (live KV caching and extended eval retention beyond 90 days) are currently gated to Elastic or Dedicated tiers because of resource isolation. However, tracing and function/tool calling are add-ons available on Compact Plus. We can map your must-haves to a custom Compact Plus with add-ons for the pilot.

3) Pricing: Attached pricing table shows list vs pilot (30% off list for a 3-month pilot on Compact Plus). The SOW draft includes the pilot length, acceptance criteria, and a single-downgrade clause.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop in Marissa to confirm DocuSign timeline and any procurement rubric.
- If procurement needs a contract exhibit that limits downgrade to one allowed change at 60 days, we can commit to that in the SOW.
- If you want a 45-day lock-in instead, we can do that but reduce the pilot discount to 25%.

If that sounds OK, I’ll send an updated SOW that locks the downgrade policy and finalizes the pricing table.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Table_Q4.xlsx, SOW_draft_Clearline_v3.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options for pilot — questions on flexibility and downgrade path

Lukas / Marissa — quick internal note while we finalize:

- Downgrade mechanics: administrative credit is fine, but Ops flagged that "one permitted downgrade" needs a clearer definition (what counts as a downgrade: seat count, feature flag, or full tier?). Recommend language: "downgrade = move from Compact Plus to Compact; feature toggles do not constitute a downgrade." That reduces ambiguity.

- Pricing anchoring: Anna asked about a pilot discount. We can do 30% for 3 months but recommend we anchor to a minimum renewal commitment (e.g., 9 months post-pilot) in case they convert. Alternatively, offer 30% on pilot with an explicit escape hatch: if they convert within 30 days after pilot, we apply a conversion credit equal to 15% of pilot spend. Both protect revenue and give Clearline flexibility.

- Add-on gating: if we allow live KV caching as a temporary pilot add-on, Ops needs a performance/incident escalation clause and a one-week rollback window. Suggest we include a 2-hour support response SLA for pilot-critical incidents.

Marissa — can you confirm procurement/DocuSign timing and whether we should include the conversion-credit language or require a minimum renewal? Also tag legal if needed for the downgrade-definition wording.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Packaging Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily@clearlinehealth.com>, ProcureTeam <procure@clearlinehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options for pilot — tradeoffs and approval path

Anna — quick consolidated update and a concrete ask to move to signature:

Summary of what we can commit for the Q4 3-month pilot (attached SOW + pricing table):
- Pilot bundle: Compact Plus (adds tracing + function calling) + temporary live KV caching add-on for pilot only.
- Pilot price: 30% off list for three months (see attached table).
- Downgrade policy: One allowed downgrade from Compact Plus to Compact during the 12-month term; the pilot has a 60-day lock-in. Downgrade defined as moving between named tiers (Compact Plus -> Compact). Feature toggles (on/off) are not considered downgrades. Downgrade triggers prorated credits on remaining committed spend; we apply an administrative credit on the invoice to zero out retro-billing adjustments.
- Conversion protection: If you convert to a term contract within 30 days after pilot, we will apply a conversion credit equal to 15% of pilot spend toward the first term invoice. If you prefer a guaranteed renewal, we can instead include a 9-month minimum post-pilot commitment (let us know which you prefer).
- SLAs for pilot add-ons: 2-hour response for pilot-critical incidents; one-week rollback window for live KV caching if we observe unacceptable degradation.

Next steps:
1) Review attached SOW_draft_Clearline_v3.pdf (I updated the downgrade definition and added the conversion-credit option).
2) If ProcureTeam is happy, sign via DocuSign (link: https://docusign.net/link/SOW_Clearline_v3).
3) Confirm kickoff date (we propose 2026-12-06) and provide your technical POC for the KV caching rollout.

If you want, I can swap the conversion-credit for the 9-month guaranteed renewal before we send to procurement — say the word.

Thanks again — excited to get Clearline into a pilot.

Best regards,
Lukas Meyer
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_draft_Clearline_v3.pdf, Redwood_Pricing_Table_Q4.xlsx
